title: Taming Update Drift in Asynchronous Federated Learning via Orthogonal Calibration

problem.claim: Asynchrony and data heterogeneity create inconsistent global and local learning objectives, causing global optimization trajectories to conflict with ongoing local updates.

gap.claim: Prior approaches send clients the most recent global parameters, potentially erasing locally accumulated progress and inducing model drift.

contributions.claim: OrthoFL uses orthogonal calibration to separate global and local learning progress and limit interference.
The server aggregates updates into global weights with an adaptive moving average and removes the projection of delayed global shift onto the received client update during local training.
The calibrated shift is merged into the client model for further training while preserving the closest orthogonal component of global progress.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five datasets, the authors report a 7.4 percentage-point accuracy improvement and up to a 12× speedup over the best-performing synchronous baseline.
The authors report consistent outperformance of state-of-the-art asynchronous baselines under varied delay patterns and heterogeneity scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Asynchronous federated learning integrates updates as they arrive to improve efficiency over synchronous protocols.
Asynchrony and heterogeneity create conflicts between global optimization and local updates, while latest-weight distribution can cause drift.
OrthoFL adaptively aggregates global updates and orthogonally calibrates delayed global shifts before merging them into client models.
The authors report improved accuracy, substantial speedup, and consistent gains over asynchronous baselines across varied conditions.

source_observation.claim: Removing the projection of delayed global progress onto the received client update is reported to reduce interference between global and local learning.

interpretation.claim: Separating update directions may help preserve local progress while incorporating compatible global progress in asynchronous optimization.

application.claim: In asynchronous distributed optimization, consider projecting delayed global changes away from directions represented by current local updates before applying them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this calibration is beneficial outside the reported datasets, delay patterns, or heterogeneity scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the five datasets or evaluation metrics beyond accuracy and speedup.
The specific adaptive moving-average rule and calibration implementation details are not provided.
The reported experimental baselines, delay patterns, heterogeneity settings, and statistical variability are unspecified.
